item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe, the true histone relatives are the histone-fold proteins: they are in class a, All alpha proteins; fold a.22, Histone fold; and the Histone-fold superfamily a.22.1. That superfamily contains nucleosome/core histones as one family and several non-nucleosomal histone-fold families, including archaeal histones and histone-fold transcription-factor subunits such as TBP-associated TAFs and NF-Y/CCAAT-binding factor subunits. Being in a.22.1 means they share the characteristic three-helix histone-fold core and are treated as homologous or plausibly homologous at the superfamily level, but the non-histone TAF/NF-Y proteins are not members of the nucleosome core histone family and their transcription-complex functions should not be transferred from H2A/H2B/H3/H4 just because the fold is shared. More distant proteins that merely form all-alpha bundles, or DNA-binding proteins only described as histone-like by function or charge, should be kept at fold/class-level similarity at most unless SCOPe places them in a.22.1; such fold/class matches are structural-template evidence, not evidence for common ancestry or detailed function transfer. Representative structures should therefore be selected from the matching SCOPe family when modeling a particular histone subtype, and from the a.22.1 superfamily only for the conserved histone-fold core.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
